issue.title: [Web] Public radio does not connect and listener may fail with regular desktop publishers
issue.body:
## Problem

The public radio session is not connecting in the Flutter Web version at:

`https://sonicrelay.hugodotnet.dev`

The signaling WebSocket appears to open successfully and the app navigates to `/listener`, but the WebRTC connection/audio never becomes usable.

Because the public radio uses the same listener/WebRTC path, this may also mean that the Web client cannot connect correctly to a regular SonicRelay desktop publisher.

## Evidence

Observed in the browser console when joining the public radio session:

```text
[SonicRelay/Waiting] start sessionId=0b1e5a7a-0000-4000-8000-000000000002
[SonicRelay/Waiting] signaling opened -> navigating to /listener
```

The sequence repeats multiple times, without reaching a usable connected/listening state.

There is also a rate-limit response during the flow:

```text
XHR POST https://sonicrelay-api.hugodotnet.dev/api/devices/token
HTTP/3 429
```

The `429` may be related to repeated device-token requests/reconnection attempts, but it should be investigated instead of assumed to be the root cause.

A large number of foreground/background events are also logged on Web:

```text
[SonicRelay/Background] app foreground=false (serviceRunning=false)
[SonicRelay/Background] app foreground=true (serviceRunning=false)
```

More Logs:
```text
Injecting <script> tag. Using callback. [flutter_bootstrap.js:1:2533](https://sonicrelay.hugodotnet.dev/flutter_bootstrap.js)
[SonicRelay/Waiting] start sessionId=0b1e5a7a-0000-4000-8000-000000000002 [main.dart.js:30383:78](https://sonicrelay.hugodotnet.dev/main.dart.js)

Navigated to https://sonicrelay.hugodotnet.dev/#/listener
[SonicRelay/Background] app foreground=false (serviceRunning=false) 2 [main.dart.js:30383:78](https://sonicrelay.hugodotnet.dev/main.dart.js)
Injecting <script> tag. Using callback. [flutter_bootstrap.js:1:2533](https://sonicrelay.hugodotnet.dev/flutter_bootstrap.js)
[SonicRelay/Background] app foreground=false (serviceRunning=false) [main.dart.js:30383:78](https://sonicrelay.hugodotnet.dev/main.dart.js)
[SonicRelay/Background] app foreground=true (serviceRunning=false) [main.dart.js:30383:78](https://sonicrelay.hugodotnet.dev/main.dart.js)

[SonicRelay/Background] app foreground=false (serviceRunning=false) [main.dart.js:30383:78](https://sonicrelay.hugodotnet.dev/main.dart.js)
```

These may be causing lifecycle-triggered reconnect/reinitialization loops in the browser.

## Secondary issue: log export on Web

Trying to export logs from the Web version also fails. The log export implementation should be checked for browser compatibility (download/blob handling, filesystem assumptions, platform-specific APIs, etc.).

## Expected behavior

- Public radio connects from Flutter Web and starts receiving audio.
- Flutter Web can connect to a normal SonicRelay desktop publisher using the same listener flow.
- Opening `/listener` does not trigger repeated signaling/device-token initialization loops.
- `/api/devices/token` is not called repeatedly enough to hit `429` during a normal connection flow.
- Lifecycle events on Web do not incorrectly restart/recreate the listener connection.
- Log export works in supported browsers.

## Investigation checklist

- [ ] Reproduce public radio connection from the production Web build.
- [ ] Test the Web listener against a regular Windows desktop publisher.
- [ ] Inspect signaling messages after the WebSocket opens: `viewer.ready`, offer, answer and ICE candidates.
- [ ] Log `RTCPeerConnection.connectionState`, `iceConnectionState`, `iceGatheringState` and `signalingState` on Web.
- [ ] Verify whether `/listener` initialization runs more than once for the same session.
- [ ] Verify whether Web lifecycle/visibility changes are causing reconnect or token regeneration.
- [ ] Check why `POST /api/devices/token` returns `429` and whether the client retries it unnecessarily.
- [ ] Verify ICE server configuration and TURN credentials received by the Web client.
- [ ] Verify browser autoplay/audio playback requirements after receiving the remote track.
- [ ] Fix/export logs using a Web-compatible download implementation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Public radio plays successfully on Flutter Web in at least Chrome/Chromium and Firefox.
- [ ] Web client successfully receives audio from a regular desktop publisher.
- [ ] A single join attempt creates only the required signaling/listener initialization flow.
- [ ] Normal connection does not produce `429` from `/api/devices/token`.
- [ ] WebRTC reaches `connected`/`completed` and the remote audio track is rendered/played.
- [ ] Export logs works on Web without platform/filesystem errors.

[SonicRelay/Waiting] start sessionId=0b1e5a7a-0000-4000-8000-000000000002
[SonicRelay/Waiting] signaling opened -> navigating to /listener
```

The sequence repeats multiple times, without reaching a usable connected/listening state.

There is also a rate-limit response during the flow:

```text
XHR POST https://sonicrelay-api.hugodotnet.dev/api/devices/token
HTTP/3 429
```

The `429` may be related to repeated device-token requests/reconnection attempts, but it should be investigated instead of assumed to be the root cause.

A large number of foreground/background events are also logged on Web:

```text
[SonicRelay/Background] app foreground=false (serviceRunning=false)
[SonicRelay/Background] app foreground=true (serviceRunning=false)
```

These may be causing lifecycle-triggered reconnect/reinitialization loops in the browser.

## Secondary issue: log export on Web

Trying to export logs from the Web version also fails. The log export implementation should be checked for browser compatibility (download/blob handling, filesystem assumptions, platform-specific APIs, etc.).

## Expected behavior

- Public radio connects from Flutter Web and starts receiving audio.
- Flutter Web can connect to a normal SonicRelay desktop publisher using the same listener flow.
- Opening `/listener` does not trigger repeated signaling/device-token initialization loops.
- `/api/devices/token` is not called repeatedly enough to hit `429` during a normal connection flow.
- Lifecycle events on Web do not incorrectly restart/recreate the listener connection.
- Log export works in supported browsers.

## Investigation checklist

- [ ] Reproduce public radio connection from the production Web build.
- [ ] Test the Web listener against a regular Windows desktop publisher.
- [ ] Inspect signaling messages after the WebSocket opens: `viewer.ready`, offer, answer and ICE candidates.
- [ ] Log `RTCPeerConnection.connectionState`, `iceConnectionState`, `iceGatheringState` and `signalingState` on Web.
- [ ] Verify whether `/listener` initialization runs more than once for the same session.
- [ ] Verify whether Web lifecycle/visibility changes are causing reconnect or token regeneration.
- [ ] Check why `POST /api/devices/token` returns `429` and whether the client retries it unnecessarily.
- [ ] Verify ICE server configuration and TURN credentials received by the Web client.
- [ ] Verify browser autoplay/audio playback requirements after receiving the remote track.
- [ ] Fix/export logs using a Web-compatible download implementation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Public radio plays successfully on Flutter Web in at least Chrome/Chromium and Firefox.
- [ ] Web client successfully receives audio from a regular desktop publisher.
- [ ] A single join attempt creates only the required signaling/listener initialization flow.
- [ ] Normal connection does not produce `429` from `/api/devices/token`.
- [ ] WebRTC reaches `connected`/`completed` and the remote audio track is rendered/played.
- [ ] Export logs works on Web without platform/filesystem errors.
